nodes.label: Category parity across language tracks
nodes.rationale: Category parity across languages is a choice, not an enforced rule. Python/Java share the same 14 category keys; C++ ships its own smaller 6-category set; Spring goes furthest with only 3 categories (dependency_injection, bean_lifecycle, configuration_profiles) with no equivalent at all in the other tracks, since categories like packaging/deployment/observability are ecosystem/tooling concepts that fit a package manager or framework better than bare language or DI-framework content. Nothing in ExerciseEngine.categories() hardcodes which categories a language 'should' have -- it's derived purely from what's present in that language's content directory, so a different-sized category set required zero app-code changes.

nodes.label: Real-toolchain verification step
nodes.rationale: The most important step when adding language content, and has caught real bugs every time it's been skipped: write the fixed solution, run it through the real engine (not a guess at output), assert success/output/contains_patterns match, and separately confirm the unedited starter code does NOT silently pass validation. Toolchain crash/error messages should be verified against actual observed stderr, not assumed.

nodes.label: Empty-Body increment() Stub Bug
nodes.rationale: increment(String name) with an empty body looks like a real method with a sensible signature but performs no side effect, leaving the metrics map permanently empty -- the same class of bug as the packaging category's service-registry exercise.

nodes.label: System.nanoTime() vs currentTimeMillis()
nodes.rationale: nanoTime() is monotonic and safe for elapsed-time measurement; currentTimeMillis() reflects wall-clock time that can jump backward if the system clock is adjusted, which could make a computed duration come out negative.

nodes.label: Empty close() Stub Bug
nodes.rationale: close() with an empty body never computes or stores the elapsed duration, so durationNanos stays null even though the Timer's construction and try-with-resources wiring are otherwise correct.

nodes.label: Always-True Stub Validator Bug
nodes.rationale: isValidPackageName returning true unconditionally never actually inspects the string, so an obviously invalid name sails through as 'valid'.

nodes.label: Empty-Body register() Stub Bug
nodes.rationale: register(name, action) with an empty body looks correct (right signature, sensible arguments, no exception) but performs no side effect, so the COMMANDS map never receives an entry and a later lookup throws NullPointerException.

nodes.label: Missing Base Case
nodes.rationale: countdown(n) never checks for a stopping condition at all, decrementing n indefinitely through and past zero until the call stack is exhausted.

nodes.label: Recursion-to-Iteration Conversion
nodes.rationale: An explicit loop uses exactly one stack frame regardless of iteration count, replacing 'combine results as calls return' with 'accumulate a running value as iterations proceed'.

nodes.label: JVM Has No Tail-Call Optimization
nodes.rationale: There is no tail-call handling in the JVM specification, so every recursive call consumes a real stack frame regardless of the call's shape.

nodes.label: O(n^2) String Concatenation Bug
nodes.rationale: result += i inside a loop re-copies the entire string built so far on every iteration, so total copying work across n iterations sums to O(n^2) even though the final string is only O(n) characters -- the same quadratic-blowup shape as Python's list-concatenation-in-recursion trap covered elsewhere in this app.

nodes.label: java.util.Objects.equals
